articles.text:
Church & Dwight Announces $225 Million Investment In BALI Hair Care Business
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 4:19 PM
Church & Dwight Announces $225 Million Investment In BALI Hair Care Business
Church & Dwight has agreed to acquire 45% of BALI Treatment for approximately $225 million, adding an investment in the European hair care and styling company behind BALI CURLS and BALI GENTS.
The agreement includes an option to acquire the remaining 55% beginning two years after closing.
The transaction is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027, subject to regulatory clearance and customary conditions.
BALI reported approximately $100 million in net sales for the 12 months ended October 31, 2026.
Founded in 2022 by Hendrik Genotte, the business develops products for curly and textured hair and has expanded into men’s grooming.
Its brands have established positions in Germany and Austria, with broader European expansion underway.
Products include Hydrating Curl Cream, Curl Defining Gel, Moisturizing Conditioner and Nourishing Shampoo. The company emphasizes vegan and cruelty-free formulations and a creator-led relationship with consumers.
Church & Dwight plans to use its international capabilities to expand distribution beyond BALI’s current concentration in a limited number of European markets.
CEO Rick Dierker said the investment aligns with the company’s preference for asset-light brands with strong category positions and the potential to improve growth and gross margins.
Church & Dwight expects the investment to be accretive to cash earnings in 2027, including acquisition-related costs and interest expense.
The structure gives the company an initial minority stake and a potential path to full ownership, while BALI gains access to a larger consumer products organization.
Church & Dwight’s existing portfolio spans household and personal care brands, including ARM & HAMMER, BATISTE, WATERPIK, THERABREATH and HERO.
The investment extends its international growth strategy into a younger hair care business with established regional demand.
KEY QUOTES
“BALI CARE grew from my own experience with curly hair and a desire to create products that help people embrace their natural curls. We are excited to partner with Church & Dwight, whose global capabilities and shared passion for innovation and consumer-focused solutions will help us bring our products and community to even more people around the world.”
Hendrik Genotte, Founder Of BALI Care
“Our investment in BALI CARE represents an important step in our strategy to accelerate international growth through high-performing, asset-light consumer brands with strong category leadership. BALI CARE has built distinctive brands with strong consumer loyalty and significant growth potential. With distribution today concentrated in a limited number of European markets, we are poised to leverage Church & Dwight’s global capabilities to expand the brands’ reach and support their next phase of growth.
“The BALI CARE investment squarely fits into our acquisition criteria that focuses on (1) #1 or #2 brand in a category; (2) asset-light; (3) expected to be growth accretive to the Company; and (4) expected to be gross margin accretive to the Company. Our strong balance sheet will continue to provide the flexibility to add additional high-quality acquisition and investment opportunities. This capability has been a key driver of Church & Dwight’s consistently strong shareholder returns.”

articles.snippet:
Nextchem has signed a binding agreement to acquire liquefied natural gas process technologies from Chart Industries for $220 million in cash. The transaction will be completed through Nextchem USA and is expected to close by the end of 2026 or in early January 2027, subject to customary regulatory approvals. Chart Industries is a wholly owned subsidiary of Baker Hughes.
The post Nextchem To Acquire LNG Technologies For $220 Million appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Nextchem To Acquire LNG Technologies For $220 Million
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 7:39 AM
Nextchem To Acquire LNG Technologies For $220 Million
Nextchem has signed a binding agreement to acquire liquefied natural gas process technologies from Chart Industries for $220 million in cash. The transaction will be completed through Nextchem USA and is expected to close by the end of 2026 or in early January 2027, subject to customary regulatory approvals. Chart Industries is a wholly owned subsidiary of Baker Hughes.
The acquisition will give Nextchem immediate access to established LNG liquefaction technologies, customer references, an existing backlog, a project pipeline, and a specialized engineering team.
Expanding Nextchem’s LNG Technology Portfolio
The transaction includes Integrated Pre-Cooled Single Mixed Refrigerant technology, its advanced IPSMR+ versions, early-stage IPDMR technology, and a portfolio of small-scale LNG processes.
Nextchem will also acquire more than 90 patents, trademarks, proprietary processes, and technical knowledge. Twelve professionals specializing in process engineering, business development, and commissioning are expected to join the company.
IPSMR is designed for mid-scale LNG projects with capacities ranging from approximately 0.5 million to two million tonnes per annum for each train. Its primary target range is between 1.4 million and two million tonnes.
The early-stage IPDMR platform is intended to extend Nextchem’s offering to larger projects with capacities ranging from approximately two million to more than four million tonnes per annum per train.
Small-scale LNG technologies included in the acquisition address applications below 0.5 million tonnes per annum. These include peak-shaving facilities, remote or stranded gas resources, alternative fuels, and locations without pipeline infrastructure.
Established Operations And Project Pipeline
The IPSMR platform has approximately 14 million tonnes per annum of historical operating references. Another 57 million tonnes is under construction, including a residual backlog of 30 million tonnes.
The technology has also been selected for approximately 90 million tonnes per annum of projects that have not yet reached a final investment decision.
Nextchem will gain capabilities across the project lifecycle, from feasibility studies and process design through licensing, detailed engineering, commissioning, start-up, and performance testing.
A 10-year supply agreement with Chart Industries will provide cold boxes for IPSMR projects. Cold boxes contain heat exchangers, piping, and other equipment used to cool natural gas until it becomes liquid.
The $220 million purchase price will be paid at closing and financed through dedicated credit facilities fully underwritten by BPER Banca. The price reflects a high-single-digit multiple of projected 2027 EBITDA.
Nextchem expects the acquired licensing operation to generate at least $25 million in EBITDA during 2027, with potential additional contributions from equipment sales and broader MAIRE revenue opportunities. The acquisition is expected to increase MAIRE’s EBITDA margin.

articles.title: Midwest startups raise $213.5 million in a week. Where is the money going?
articles.snippet: Midwest startups raise $213.5 million in a week. Where is the money going? Techli
articles.text:
Four of six deals are reported in Chicago, and the region is experiencing the latest funding activity in the form of investments in AI infrastructure and financial services.
According to StartMidwest’s funding roundup , $213.5 million was raised in six deals by Midwest startups and financial technology companies during the week ending Nov. 6, with two $100 million rounds accounting for almost all the capital.
Ocient, an AI infrastructure firm in Chicago, and Erebor Bank, which is based in Columbus, Ohio, were the leaders of the activity. The remaining included health care technology, artificial intelligence and fintech firms, reflecting the diversity of sectors that are being invested in all over the region.
The headline figure, however, requires some qualification: Erebor Bank’s $100 million investment from Japan’s SBI Holdings was announced as a planned commitment, not a completed financing round. The difference is important in evaluating the amount of capital that actually has flowed to companies in the Midwest.
The biggest round up to date was Ocient’s $100 million Series C , which was announced on November 5. The investment, led by BOKA Capital and OCA Ventures, totals $260 million for the Chicago firm. Other investors who were on board included existing investors Greycroft, In-Q-Tel, Blue Bear Capital, Buoyant Ventures, PSP Growth, Pritzker Group Venture Capital and Eron Wolf. Dallas Venture Capital joined as a new investor.
Ocient is a company that creates data analytics and AI solutions for enterprises dealing with vast amounts of data. The new investment will allow it to continue developing its OcientAIQ solutions that enable enterprises to deploy AI agents and analytics in petabyte-scale data environments.
Reliable, governed data is becoming a key infrastructure need as businesses delve into agentic AI systems that can analyze information and execute tasks. Ocient claims its solution can be used for data governance along with high-performance data analytics, enabling AI agents and analysts to ask questions about the data in a customer’s environment.
The company anticipates that its revenue will more than triple in 2026 due to the demand of customers with growing and high-volume data sets. This projection is not a financial result but an estimate by Ocient.
The second $100 million was from a digital bank called Erebor Bank, based in Columbus, Ohio, which offers services to companies in fields such as artificial intelligence, robotics and advanced manufacturing, defense, and energy. The timing of the completion of the investment was not mentioned in the funding roundup, but SBI Holdings revealed its plan to invest $100 million .
Four of the six transactions were in Chicago. In addition to Ocient, medical technology firm Focused Medical Technologies, a treatment developer for pulmonary embolism, secured $6 million in investment, including two medical technology strategic investors and UCM Ventures. The University of Chicago startup is targeting the funds for product development, manufacturing and setting up for a pivotal study in the United States.
Consumer insights firm QualSights raised $5 million in funding, led by Duo Partners. The company employs smart sensors and a consumer application and AI analytics to provide a better understanding of how humans use physical products. The funding came with the appointment of Prasanna Pitale as Chief Executive.

articles.title: Square Nine Capital Leads $206 Million Financing For Aline Accounting Partners
articles.snippet:
Square Nine Capital has led a $206 million financing for Aline Accounting Partners, supporting debt refinancing, near-term acquisitions and continued expansion of the accounting and professional services platform.
The post Square Nine Capital Leads $206 Million Financing For Aline Accounting Partners appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Square Nine Capital Leads $206 Million Financing For Aline Accounting Partners
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 1:03 PM
Square Nine Capital Leads $206 Million Financing For Aline Accounting Partners
Square Nine Capital has led a $206 million financing for Aline Accounting Partners, supporting debt refinancing, near-term acquisitions and continued expansion of the accounting and professional services platform.
The financing consists of a revolving credit facility, a term loan and a delayed draw term loan facility.
Proceeds refinanced existing indebtedness and provided growth capital for acquisitions. The facilities also support Aline’s broader strategy of investing in talent, technology and additional service capabilities.
Aline was formed in August 2024 through the merger of three firms with established operating histories. Its model combines local accounting and advisory relationships with shared business resources.
Member firms receive support across finance and reporting, information technology, human resources, recruiting, staffing, marketing, growth and mergers and acquisitions.
The organization intends to use those shared capabilities to strengthen collaboration, improve operating efficiency and expand what its teams can provide to clients.
CEO Matt Lender said the financing supports Aline’s long-term strategy and will help incoming firms gain resources to develop their businesses.
Square Nine provides flexible capital to middle-market companies, partnering with founders, owners, management teams and financial sponsors.
Its investments support acquisitions, growth, refinancings, recapitalizations and other strategic transactions across different parts of a company’s capital structure.
The Aline transaction combines funding for immediate balance sheet needs with capacity for additional acquisitions. That structure supports both the existing organization and firms joining its network.
Polsinelli served as legal counsel to Aline. Paul Hastings advised Square Nine.
The financing gives Aline additional resources as it develops a platform built around established accounting practices, local client relationships and centralized support functions. Square Nine’s principals said the arrangement provides flexibility for continued expansion and investment in the organization’s capabilities.
KEY QUOTES
“Aline has built a strong foundation for growth by bringing together established accounting firms and investing in the resources that help them thrive. We are pleased to lead a financing that supports these acquisitions and provides flexibility for continued expansion. We look forward to partnering with Aline team as the organization grows and expands its capabilities.”
Christopher Brown And Griffin Coakley, Principals At Square Nine Capital
“This financing marks an important milestone for Aline. Square Nine understood our business and delivered a financing solution that supports our long-term strategy. We are excited to welcome the new firms to Aline and provide their teams with additional resources to grow, broaden their capabilities and continue delivering exceptional service to their clients.”
Matt Lender, CEO Of Aline Accounting Partners

The transaction comes as the registered investment advisory firm approaches $17 billion in assets under management after completing 26 acquisitions since its founding in 2023.

articles.text:
Modern Wealth Management: $200 Million Centerbridge Investment To Accelerate Growth Of $17 Billion RIA Platform
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 9:32 AM
Modern Wealth Management: $200 Million Centerbridge Investment To Accelerate Growth Of $17 Billion RIA Platform
Modern Wealth Management has secured a $200 million hybrid debt-and-equity investment from funds managed by Centerbridge Partners to support additional acquisitions and expansion of its national wealth management platform. The transaction comes as the registered investment advisory firm approaches $17 billion in assets under management after completing 26 acquisitions since its founding in 2023.
Funds managed by Harvest Partners SCF also participated in the investment.
Crestview Partners, which provided Modern Wealth’s initial $200 million equity financing in 2023, will remain the firm’s largest institutional investor.
The financing preserves continuity with the existing ownership group while introducing additional capital to support the company’s expansion strategy.
Modern Wealth will also remain majority employee-owned.
The company currently has more than 150 employee shareholders.
Founded in April 2023, Modern Wealth was established by Gary Roth, Mike Capelle, Jason Gordo, and Jason Del Col.
The firm has grown through a combination of acquisitions and organic expansion.
Its operating model focuses on integrating established financial advisory businesses into a platform providing centralized technology, operations, and specialized planning services.
Modern Wealth serves clients through investment management, financial planning, tax planning and preparation, estate planning, and other wealth management capabilities.
The company believes these services allow advisors to address increasingly complex financial needs while maintaining relationships with their clients.
Its acquisition strategy emphasizes partnerships with independent advisory firms seeking additional operational resources and opportunities for long-term growth.
Acquired businesses gain access to the firm’s technology, investment expertise, and centralized support infrastructure.
Modern Wealth intends to use the new investment to expand its presence in important wealth management markets while continuing to pursue additional acquisitions.
The capital will also support development of its integrated planning and advisory platform.
The firm has established an Organic Growth Hub and Advisor Support Center designed to help financial advisors strengthen customer relationships and business development activities.
These resources provide support involving marketing, technology, operations, and specialized financial planning.
Management believes that centralizing certain activities can allow advisors to devote more time to client service and organic growth.
The latest investment comes approximately three and a half years after the firm’s launch.
During that period, Modern Wealth has completed 26 acquisitions and expanded its assets under management to nearly $17 billion.
The company’s growth reflects an ongoing trend within the registered investment advisory industry toward consolidation and the development of larger independent wealth management platforms.
Advisory firms are increasingly seeking access to technology, compliance resources, succession planning solutions, and specialized professional expertise.

articles.text:
Asset Based Lending Announces Fourth Securitization of $200 Million, Marking Largest Transaction to Date
News provided by
Asset Based Lending, LLC
Nov 12, 2026, 13:33 ET
Share this article
Share this article
JERSEY CITY, N.J. , Nov. 12, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Asset Based Lending (ABL) , a national private lender and a driving force behind the next generation of real estate investment, has successfully closed its fourth unrated securitization, totaling $200 million. The transaction, ABL 2026 RTL-1, which priced on October 15 and closed on October 26, marks ABL's largest to date, bringing its cumulative securitization volume to $723 million.
The transaction is backed by a diversified pool of business-purpose residential real estate loans, with an industry-leading concentration of ground-up infill construction loans. This reflects ABL's 16 years of experience in ground-up construction lending and its proven ability to manage the complexities and risks of residential development.
"We are proud to lead the industry in financing ground-up construction, and to do it at a cost that keeps our pricing competitive for the builders we serve," said Kevin Rodman, CEO of ABL. "This transaction underscores the strength of the platform our team has built and the confidence investors have in our credit. Every one of these loans puts new housing on the ground."
The transaction also demonstrates ABL's ability to navigate challenging market conditions. Despite heightened volatility and increased investor selectivity across the securitization market, ABL secured competitive financing terms. The deal reached the market in approximately three weeks, making it one of the company's fastest securitization executions.
Performance Trust Capital Partners, LLC served as structuring agent, with Nomura Securities International, Inc. ("Nomura") and Mizuho Securities USA LLC serving as joint bookrunners.
"Successfully executing this transaction amid market volatility reinforces the effectiveness of our capital markets strategy and the quality of our platform," said Daniel Gotay, Head of Capital Markets at ABL. "We have built durable relationships with institutional investors and established a track record they can underwrite, giving us consistent access to capital. For our borrowers, that is what matters most: they can count on ABL to fund their projects from start to finish."
The securitization also reflects ABL's expanding national footprint, with collateral spanning the Northeast, Sun Belt, Rust Belt and South. This geographic diversification supports the company's strategy to continue growing beyond its established Northeast presence and finance residential development in markets across the country.
To learn more about ABL, please visit www.ablfunding.com .
About Asset Based Lending
Asset Based Lending was established in 2010, providing fast bridge financing to real estate investors for the purchase, renovation, new construction, and long-term refinance of single-family, multi-family, and mixed-use properties. A trusted lender to thousands of investors, Asset Based Lending has closed over $4.4 billion in loans since its founding. Learn more at https://www.ablfunding.com/ . Follow the company on LinkedIn .

Key Points Patrick raised its dividend while merger covenants block use of the renewed buyback…

Patrick raised its dividend while merger covenants block use of the renewed buyback capacity.
The repurchase authorization sits idle because the pending LCI merger restricts Patrick from buying its own stock.
Patrick balances shareholder returns against funding organic growth and acquisitions from its cash generation.
Patrick Industries ( PATK ) announced on November 13, 2026 that its board had increased the quarterly common-stock dividend to $0.52 per share from $0.47 and replenished its share-repurchase authorization to $200 million. The announcement pairs a higher cash payout with additional repurchase capacity that cannot currently be used because of covenants in Patrick’s pending all-stock merger with LCI Industries ( LCII ) .
The board approved the dividend increase on November 11, 2026. The new rate is approximately 10.6% above the previous rate, calculated from the announced per-share amounts. The dividend is payable on December 7, 2026, to shareholders of record at the close of business on November 23, 2026.
Repurchase Capacity Remains Restricted
The authorization covers repurchases over the next 24 months and includes $61.9 million that remained under the previous authorization. The board therefore added $138.1 million of capacity, calculated as the difference between the new total and the remaining amount.
The repurchase program cannot presently be used. Patrick entered into the LCI merger agreement on June 30, 2026, and its operating covenants restrict repurchases of Patrick common stock. The company expects those restrictions to remain in place while the agreement is in effect.
The restrictions were already visible in Patrick’s third-quarter report , which said the company made no share repurchases during the quarter because of the merger agreement. The SEC declared the merger registration statement effective on October 19, 2026, and Patrick has scheduled a special shareholder meeting for November 18, 2026.
Cash Flow and Capital Allocation
Chief Executive Officer Andy Nemeth said the decisions were grounded in Patrick’s capital allocation, cash generation and balance sheet. “Since initiating our quarterly dividend in 2019, we have raised it each year and have been active with share repurchases, deploying $106.1 million in the first nine months of 2026,” he said.
Returning capital is only one use of that cash. Nemeth said cash generation through the cycle also enables investment in organic initiatives and strategic mergers and acquisitions, which Patrick expects to remain a priority.
The latest results provide context for those competing demands. Third-quarter net sales were $975 million, compared with $976 million a year earlier, while operating income declined to $50 million from $66 million. For the first nine months of 2026, operating cash flow was $147 million, down from $199 million in the prior-year period. Patrick attributed the change to working-capital deployment supporting its composite-products growth strategy and inventory management for customers.
